questions.prompt: Which pass rate should a regression eval have, per Anthropic?

options.text: Low at first, so it gives the team a hill to climb
options.explanation: That describes capability evals. They start at a low pass rate.

options.text: About 50%, so there is still room to improve
options.explanation: Regression evals protect what already works, so they aim much higher than that.

options.text: Nearly 100%, since a drop means something is broken
options.explanation: Right. Regression evals ask whether the agent still handles everything it used to.

questions.prompt: What does it mean to "graduate" a task, in Anthropic's post?

options.text: Move a reliably passing task from capability to regression
options.explanation: Right. The question changes from "can we do this at all?" to "can we still do this reliably?"

options.text: Delete a task after the agent passes it for the first time
options.explanation: Passing tasks are kept. They guard against future breakage.

options.text: Move a failing task out of the regression suite until it is fixed
options.explanation: That would hide the regression. Graduation goes from capability to regression, not the other way.

questions.prompt: Which Gemini model option do the docs advise most production apps to use?

options.text: A `latest` alias, so you always get the newest release
options.explanation: The docs warn that this alias is hot-swapped with every new release of the model.

options.text: An experimental model, to get the newest features first
options.explanation: The docs say experimental models are typically not suitable for production and may change availability.

options.text: A specific stable model, which usually doesn't change
options.explanation: Right. The docs say most production apps should use a specific stable model.
